questions: If a file with the same name already exists in the target directory, should the move operation overwrite it, raise an error, or skip the file?
Should the function move files from subdirectories of the source directory, or only files directly in the source directory?
If the target directory is created, should its parent directories also be created if they don't exist (i.e., use os.makedirs with exist_ok=True)?
Should the function preserve the directory structure of moved files (e.g., keep subdirectory paths) or flatten all files into the target directory?
If moving a file fails (e.g., permission error), should the function abort and return the count so far, continue skipping that file, or raise an exception?
Does the pattern match against the full file path (including directory names) or only the base filename?
Should the function follow symbolic links to directories when traversing the source directory?
If the source directory exists but is empty, should the function return 0 immediately, or still attempt to traverse?
